concepts.title: Arithmetic Operators: Floor Division, Modulo, Exponent
concepts.definition: Beyond the four familiar operations, Python offers three special arithmetic tools: // keeps only the whole-number part of a quotient, % hands back the leftover after division, and ** raises a base to a power. For any division, quotient times divisor plus remainder always rebuilds the dividend.
concepts.key_idea: // drops the decimals, % keeps what // threw away, and ** repeats multiplication.
question_patterns: find the value of 13 % 5 and 13 // 5 in Python
what is the output of 3 ** 4 in the Python shell
evaluate 5 // 2 and 2 // 5 and explain the difference in results
for dividend 23 and divisor 4, compute quotient, remainder and verify quotient * divisor + remainder
which operator returns the remainder of a division in Python
predict the output of print(4.00/(2.0+2.0))

solution_steps.explain: floor division // removes the decimal part of the quotient
the modulo operator % returns what remains after the whole quotient is removed

solution_steps.action: rebuild the dividend as a check
solution_steps.explain: quotient * divisor + remainder must reproduce the original dividend

worked_examples.q: What does 17 // 5 evaluate to in Python?

concepts.title: Operator Precedence Evaluation Order
concepts.definition: When several operators share one expression, precedence decides who acts first: parentheses beat everything, then * / // %, then + and -. Equal-precedence partners work left to right, and each step of the evaluation rewrites the expression until one number remains.
concepts.key_idea: Parentheses first, then multiply/divide, then add/subtract; ties resolve left to right.
question_patterns: how will Python evaluate the expression 20 + 30 * 40
evaluate (20 + 30) * 40 step by step and compare with 20 + 30 * 40
find the value of 15.0 / 4.0 + (8 + 3.0)
why does parenthesis override the normal precedence of operators
evaluate 2 + 9 * ((3 * 12) - 8) / 10 showing every step
state the order in which Python evaluates * and + in one expression

solution_steps.explain: the bracketed sum is evaluated before anything outside it
the / operation binds tighter than +, so it is performed next
the two prepared parts are added last to give the final value

concepts.title: Augmented Assignment Operators
concepts.definition: Shorthand operators such as +=, -=, *=, /=, //= and **= fold an arithmetic step into the assignment itself: x += y means x is replaced by x + y. Chaining two of them applies the updates one after another to the running value.
concepts.key_idea: Each augmented operator rewrites the variable in place using its own current value.
question_patterns: num1 = 4 and num2 = 3; what is num1 after num1 += num2
rewrite x += y as a plain assignment statement
starting from num1 = 2, what is num1 after num1 += 3 followed by num1 *= 2
give the output of num1 -= num2 when num1 = 10 and num2 = 2
name all the augmented assignment operators available in Python
num1 = 4; predict the printed value after num1 **= 2 + 1

solution_steps.explain: += adds the increment to the variable's current value and stores it back
*= multiplies the running value by the multiplier and stores it back

worked_examples.q: After x = 5 and x += 3, what is x?

concepts.title: Simple Interest Amount Payable
concepts.definition: When money is lent at a fixed yearly rate, the interest charged grows linearly with the principal, the rate and the time in years. The borrower returns the principal together with this interest as the amount payable.
concepts.key_idea: Interest equals principal times rate times time divided by 100; add it back to the principal to get the payable amount.
concepts.textbook_ref: keip103.txt Exercise Q6 and compound-interest function example (lines 853-862, 1259-1264)
question_patterns: write the steps to calculate the amount payable when money is lent on simple interest

write a Python program that takes principal, rate and time as input and prints the payable amount

solution_steps.explain: principal, yearly rate and years in years multiply together, then division by 100 converts the rate percent

solution_steps.action: add the interest to the loan
solution_steps.explain: the payable amount is the original principal plus the earned interest

worked_examples.q: Find the simple interest on Rs 5000 at 8 percent per year for 2 years, in rupees.

concepts.title: range Function Loop Count and Last Value
concepts.definition: range([start], stop[, step]) produces the integers from start up to but excluding stop, spaced by step. The number of values it yields is the smallest count of steps that reaches or crosses stop, and the last printed value sits one step short of stop.
concepts.key_idea: Count the iterations with an upward rounded division, then add (count - 1) steps to the start to land on the final value printed.
concepts.textbook_ref: keip103.txt section 3.12.1, Example 3.13 and Exercise Q11 (lines 1080-1108, 1274-1277)

solution_steps.explain: divide the span rounded upward by the step to get how many values appear
the last value is start advanced by (loop_count - 1) steps of the given size

concepts.title: Nested Loop Print Count
concepts.definition: A loop placed inside another loop is called nested: for every single pass of the outer loop, the inner loop finishes all of its own passes. The total number of inner-body executions is therefore the product of the two iteration counts.
concepts.key_idea: Outer pass count times inner pass count gives how many times the innermost statement runs.
question_patterns: how many times is the inner print executed when the outer loop runs 3 times and the inner loop 2 times
count the total lines printed by Program 3-6 including the Out of outer loop message

how many times does the message Out of inner loop appear in Program 3-6
if the inner body prints 2 lines, how many lines appear inside the loops for 3 outer passes

solution_steps.action: count the lines produced in one outer pass
solution_steps.explain: each outer pass prints the inner values plus one Out of inner loop message, so inner_count + 1 lines

solution_steps.action: scale by the number of outer passes
solution_steps.explain: the outer loop repeats that block outer_count times
one final Out of outer loop line appears after both loops end

worked_examples.q: An outer loop runs 4 times and an inner loop runs 3 times per pass. How many times does the innermost statement execute?

concepts.title: Choosing Python Data Types
concepts.definition: Every value in Python carries a type: int for whole counts, float for measurements with decimals, bool for the two truth constants True and False, complex for imaginary parts, str for text, list and tuple for ordered groups, and dictionary for key-value pairs. Picking the type means matching the kind of data and the operations needed.
concepts.key_idea: Counts take int, measurable quantities take float, yes/no facts take bool, and text takes str.
question_patterns: which data type will represent the number of months in a year and why
which data type suits storing whether a student is a resident of Delhi or not
why is a mobile number better stored as a string than a number
name the data type for pocket money and for the volume of a sphere
how does a tuple differ from a list in Python

solution_steps.action: ask whether the data is counted, measured, true/false or textual
solution_steps.explain: counted things are int, measured ones float, yes/no facts bool, text str

solution_steps.action: check whether several values travel together
solution_steps.explain: ordered groups use list (changeable) or tuple (fixed); labelled pairs use a dictionary
values like phone numbers or codes may look numeric but behave as strings when leading zeros or lookup matter

worked_examples.q: Which data type fits a yes/no fact?

concepts.title: Syntax, Logical and Runtime Errors
concepts.definition: Program mistakes come in three kinds. Syntax errors break the language rules so the interpreter refuses to run the code at all. Logical errors run silently but produce a wrong result because the method itself is flawed. Runtime errors pass the syntax check yet abort midway, for example when a denominator turns out to be zero. Locating and fixing them is called debugging.
concepts.key_idea: Syntax stops the program before it starts, logic gives wrong answers quietly, runtime crashes mid-flight.
question_patterns: categorise 25 / 0 as syntax, logical or runtime error
why does writing 10 + 12/2 for an average show a logical error rather than a syntax error
which type of error stops a Python program before execution begins
give one example of a runtime error besides division by zero
define debugging and name the errors it removes
is a missing closing parenthesis a syntax error or a runtime error

solution_steps.action: test whether the interpreter even starts
solution_steps.explain: refusal to run with an error message signals a syntax error, like an unclosed bracket
mid-run abort means a runtime error, for example a zero denominator

solution_steps.action: test whether the answer is right
solution_steps.explain: a clean run with a wrong value exposes a logical error, such as a misplaced average formula

worked_examples.q: Which error kind stops the program before it starts?

concepts.title: if elif else Conditional Statements
concepts.definition: Conditional statements let one program take different paths depending on a test. A plain if runs its indented block only when the condition holds; if...else adds an alternative block for the failing case; the if...elif...else ladder checks several conditions in order and runs the first block whose test is true.
concepts.key_idea: The ladder tests conditions top to bottom and runs only the first true block before skipping the rest.
question_patterns: what is the difference between the else and elif constructs of the if statement
write the condition under which a program prints Eligible to vote using if
how does the interpreter choose which block of an if..elif..else ladder to execute
write a ladder that labels a number as positive, negative or zero
why is indentation important for the body of an if statement
how many elif parts may one if statement contain

solution_steps.explain: if it is true, its indented block runs and the whole ladder is left
each failing test passes control to the next elif condition in line
when no test succeeds, the else block, if present, executes

worked_examples.q: Which clause runs when every test in the ladder fails?
